intended_application: Internal task and knowledge coordination: retrieve permission-appropriate internal documents, suggest task ownership and next steps, and prepare draft action lists and reminders for human review. Do not execute client-facing commitments or financial transactions.
organization: Hypothetical small professional-services company; no real company or observed deployment is represented.
industry_sector: Professional services; internal administrative and knowledge-work coordination, not manufacturing operations.
business_need: Hypothetical objectives [H2]: reduce effort locating internal information and coordinating follow-up, and improve clarity of task ownership. No measured time saving, accuracy gain, ROI, or successful pilot is supplied.
users_stakeholders: Hypothetical stakeholders [H1]: consultants, project leads, an office administrator, a company owner, and the person responsible for document permissions and client confidentiality.
capabilities_constraints: Hypothetical premises [H1]: a shared document repository and task tracker, limited technical support, and no dedicated AI engineering team. Document consistency, permissions, access interfaces, staff review capacity, and budget are unverified. Human review is required before adopting assignments or sending reminders. Consequential client commitments and financial transactions remain subject to authorized human approval and are outside the proposed pilot execution scope.
risk_consequence_context: Hypothetical consequence context [H1]: incorrect retrieval or coordination drafts could cause missed internal follow-up, rework, or inappropriate disclosure of client information. No production-equipment or wafer-quality decision is in scope. Financial and client-facing authority remains with authorized humans. Frequency, severity, and adequacy of proposed controls are unknown; no incident history is asserted.
management_question: Should the company authorize an eight-week, read-only and draft-only Agentic AI pilot for internal task and knowledge coordination, or retain its current human-coordinated approach pending further evidence, and what evidence and human-approval conditions should be required before considering broader internal use?
time_horizon: Decision now on a proposed eight-week bounded internal pilot; broader internal use requires a separate review. Client commitments and financial transactions are not authorized by this decision.

SHARED TECHNOLOGY DEFINITION
Agentic AI means a bounded class of integrated, model-directed systems that select tool-mediated actions and use environmental feedback to pursue delegated goals within permissions and human oversight.
This is the same technology class in both cases; neither the organization nor the proposed integration changes its definition.

CASE-SPECIFIC PREMISES
[H1] All company size, stakeholder, repository/task-tracker, limited-support, permission, authority, and consequence details in this case are stipulated hypothetical premises. Unlike the primary case, this case supplies no wafer lines or MES/ERP infrastructure. The intended scope is an approved subset of internal material, read-only retrieval, and draft-only coordination with human review. Those are proposed boundaries, not demonstrated controls or integrations. [H2] Easier retrieval and follow-up are objectives only. Current workflow performance, document quality, access readiness, staff workload, cost, and expansion thresholds are unknown. The original primary-scenario H1/H2 summary in the unchanged evidence payload does not describe this company.

EVIDENCE SCOPE NOTE
The unchanged approved payload below contains an [H1/H2] summary of the original semiconductor scenario. That line is a record of the primary scenario, not shared external evidence. C1-C5 and the shared technology definition are identical across cases. Neither case supplies comparative evidence establishing uniquely new capabilities over traditional automation, rule-based workflows, or optimization systems; do not invent those comparisons or preassign a classification.
